# Oracle CDC database setup runbook

<!-- Generated by runbook-ui: npm run export-md. Edit runbook-ui/data/runbook.ts, not this file. -->

**For:** DBAs preparing an Oracle database for Debezium LogMiner change capture into Kafka.

Run the sections in order. Each step says where to run it, whether it changes anything, what you should see, and which part of the dba_scripts files does the same job. The scripts are the source of truth: this runbook shows the same statements so you can run them one at a time and check each result.

## Before you start

- A SYSDBA login on the Oracle server, and a maintenance window if section 2 applies (it restarts the database).
- The database is a CDB with the application schema in a PDB. The commands use ORCLPDB1, EMOB, c##debezium and /u01/oracle_logs: replace them with your own values, and replace every password placeholder.
- Sections 5 and 6 list the captured tables. If that list changes, change both sections and the connector's table.include.list (section 9).

## Scripts

| Script (dba_scripts/) | What it does | Runbook |
|---|---|---|
| `dba_cdc_01_check.sql` | Read-only check of the current state | Section 1 |
| `dba_cdc_02_archivelog.sql` | Recovery area, enable ARCHIVELOG (restarts the database). Only for a database that does not archive yet | Section 2 (2.2 and 2.3) |
| `dba_cdc_03_cdc_setup.sql` | Database logging, CDC user, table grants, log groups, verification | Sections 3 to 7 |
| `dba_cdc_04_monitoring_user.sql` | Read-only user for the Grafana exporter | Section 8 |
| `dba_cdc_05_archivelog_cleanup.sh` | Scheduled, CDC-safe archive log cleanup (RMAN) | Section 10 |
| `dba_cdc_06_check_cdc_privileges.sql` | Read-only check of every privilege the CDC user needs | Step 7.2 |
| `dba_cdc_07_logminer_capture_test.sql` | Read-only test that LogMiner sees changes on the captured tables | Step 7.3 |

<a id="s1"></a>
## 1. Check the current state

Read-only. The result decides whether section 2 is needed.

<a id="s1-1"></a>
### 1.1 Read archive mode, logging, recovery area and PDBs

**read-only** · **script:** `dba_cdc_01_check.sql`

Shows what is already in place so you only run the steps that are needed.

Run in: SQL*Plus as SYSDBA

```sql
set linesize 200 pagesize 100
select name, cdb, log_mode, force_logging, supplemental_log_data_min, supplemental_log_data_all
  from v$database;

show parameter db_recovery_file_dest

select name, open_mode from v$pdbs;
```

**Expected:** CDB = YES and your PDB is READ WRITE. Note LOG_MODE.

- Whatever LOG_MODE shows, continue with [step 2.1](#s2-1): it decides which other steps of section 2 apply.

[Back to contents](#contents)

<a id="s2"></a>
## 2. Archive logging

LogMiner reads archived redo logs, and Debezium refuses to start unless a LOCAL archive destination is VALID. A production database is normally archiving already: then this section is only the read-only check in 2.1, and the existing archive setup must not be changed.

<a id="s2-1"></a>
### 2.1 Check the existing archive setup

**read-only**

Read-only. Shows whether the database already archives and whether Debezium can use the destination.

Run in: SQL*Plus as SYSDBA, connected to CDB$ROOT

```sql
set linesize 200 pagesize 100
col dest_name format a22
col destination format a40
col error format a50
select log_mode from v$database;

--main status of archive log dest checking (based on this many decisions will be taken)
select dest_id, dest_name, status, type, destination, error
  from v$archive_dest_status
 where status <> 'INACTIVE';

-- space checking
select round(space_limit/1024/1024/1024, 1)       limit_gb,
       round(space_used/1024/1024/1024, 1)        used_gb,
       round(space_reclaimable/1024/1024/1024, 1) reclaimable_gb
  from v$recovery_file_dest;
```

**Expected:** LOG_MODE = ARCHIVELOG and at least one row with TYPE = LOCAL and STATUS = VALID.

- **If ARCHIVELOG with one LOCAL destination VALID (normal for production): nothing to change. Skip the rest of section 2 and go to [step 3.1](#s3-1).**
- ARCHIVELOG with several LOCAL destinations VALID: no database change. Tell the platform team which one Debezium should read, for the connector setting log.mining.archive.destination.name (for example LOG_ARCHIVE_DEST_1).
- ARCHIVELOG but no LOCAL destination VALID (only remote or standby destinations, or one in ERROR): stop and agree a fix with the DBA team that owns the archive setup. See [step 2.4](#s2-4).
- **If NOARCHIVELOG (new or test database): do [step 2.2](#s2-2), [step 2.3](#s2-3) and [step 2.4](#s2-4).**
- **On a database that already archives, never change db_recovery_file_dest or log_archive_dest_n: backups, retention and standby databases depend on them.**

[Back to contents](#contents)

<a id="s2-2"></a>
### 2.2 Create the recovery area directory

**change** · **when:** Only if LOG_MODE = NOARCHIVELOG (a database that does not archive yet)

The OS directory must exist and belong to the oracle user before Oracle is pointed at it.

Run in: Shell on the database server, as root

```bash
mkdir -p /u01/oracle_logs
chown oracle:oinstall /u01/oracle_logs
chmod 750 /u01/oracle_logs
```

- The group name (oinstall) can differ on your server.

[Back to contents](#contents)

<a id="s2-3"></a>
### 2.3 Set the recovery area and enable ARCHIVELOG

**downtime** · **when:** Only if LOG_MODE = NOARCHIVELOG · **script:** `dba_cdc_02_archivelog.sql`

Set the size before the location. Switching the log mode needs a restart.

Run in: SQL*Plus as SYSDBA, connected to CDB$ROOT

```sql
alter system set db_recovery_file_dest_size = 15G   scope = both;
alter system set db_recovery_file_dest      = '/u01/oracle_logs' scope = both;

shutdown immediate;
startup mount;
alter database archivelog;
alter database open;

archive log list
```

**Expected:** Database log mode = Archive Mode, Automatic archival = Enabled.

- All sessions are disconnected. Schedule it and tell the application owners.

[Back to contents](#contents)

<a id="s2-4"></a>
### 2.4 Point the archive destination at the recovery area

**change** · **when:** Only after [step 2.3](#s2-3), or to repair a destination in ERROR on a database whose archive setup you own. Never on a production database that already archives

Sends archive logs to the recovery area set in the previous step, then verifies it. This also repaired an ERROR destination (ORA-16032) on the test database.

Run in: SQL*Plus as SYSDBA, connected to CDB$ROOT

```sql
select value from v$parameter where name = 'log_archive_dest_1';   -- record the current value first

alter system set log_archive_dest_1 = 'LOCATION=USE_DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST' scope = both;

select dest_id, dest_name, status, type, destination, error
  from v$archive_dest
 where dest_id = 1;
```

**Expected:** STATUS = VALID, TYPE = LOCAL, ERROR empty.

- Keep the value recorded by the first query: it is how you undo the change.
- Do not continue to [step 3.1](#s3-1) until a LOCAL destination is VALID. Re-run [step 2.1](#s2-1) to confirm.

[Back to contents](#contents)

<a id="s3"></a>
## 3. Database-level logging

Two switches for the whole database. Online, no restart.

<a id="s3-1"></a>
### 3.1 Enable minimal supplemental logging and force logging

**change** · **script:** `dba_cdc_03_cdc_setup.sql, Step 1`

Minimal supplemental logging lets LogMiner read row changes. FORCE LOGGING stops NOLOGGING operations from bypassing the redo, which CDC would miss.

Run in: SQL*Plus as SYSDBA, connected to CDB$ROOT

```sql
alter session set container = CDB$ROOT;
alter database add supplemental log data;
alter database force logging;

select supplemental_log_data_min, force_logging, log_mode from v$database;
```

**Expected:** SUPPLEMENTAL_LOG_DATA_MIN = YES, FORCE_LOGGING = YES, LOG_MODE = ARCHIVELOG.

- The per-table log groups come later, in [step 6.1](#s6-1).

[Back to contents](#contents)

<a id="s4"></a>
## 4. CDC user and privileges

A common user, because LogMiner reads the redo of the whole CDB. It gets only what Debezium needs and no broad ANY privileges.

<a id="s4-1"></a>
### 4.1 Create the CDC user

**change** · **script:** `dba_cdc_03_cdc_setup.sql, Step 2`

Common user in all containers, on the USERS tablespace.

Run in: SQL*Plus as SYSDBA, connected to CDB$ROOT

```sql
alter session set container = CDB$ROOT;

create user c##debezium identified by "<password>"
  default tablespace users
  quota unlimited on users
  container = all;
```

- The script asks for the password at run time, so it never sits in the file. Replace the placeholder with the real password, and do not save it in this document.

[Back to contents](#contents)

<a id="s4-2"></a>
### 4.2 Grant the LogMiner privileges

**change** · **script:** `dba_cdc_03_cdc_setup.sql, Step 2`

Session, LogMiner, and read access on the V$ views Debezium queries.

Run in: SQL*Plus as SYSDBA, connected to CDB$ROOT

```sql
grant create session, set container             to c##debezium container = all;
grant logmining                                 to c##debezium container = all;
grant select any transaction                    to c##debezium container = all;
grant select_catalog_role, execute_catalog_role to c##debezium container = all;
grant execute on dbms_logmnr                    to c##debezium container = all;
grant execute on dbms_logmnr_d                  to c##debezium container = all;
grant create table, create sequence             to c##debezium container = all;
grant select on v_$database                     to c##debezium container = all;
grant select on v_$log                          to c##debezium container = all;
grant select on v_$log_history                  to c##debezium container = all;
grant select on v_$logfile                      to c##debezium container = all;
grant select on v_$archived_log                 to c##debezium container = all;
grant select on v_$archive_dest_status          to c##debezium container = all;
grant select on v_$logmnr_logs                  to c##debezium container = all;
grant select on v_$logmnr_contents              to c##debezium container = all;
grant select on v_$logmnr_parameters            to c##debezium container = all;
grant select on v_$transaction                  to c##debezium container = all;
grant select on v_$mystat                       to c##debezium container = all;
grant select on v_$statname                     to c##debezium container = all;
```

- Not granted by design: SELECT ANY TABLE, FLASHBACK ANY TABLE, LOCK ANY TABLE, DBA. Access to the data tables is given per table in [step 5.1](#s5-1).

[Back to contents](#contents)

<a id="s5"></a>
## 5. Read access on the captured tables

Debezium reads the 18 captured tables for the initial schema and for flashback. Grant on those tables only.

<a id="s5-1"></a>
### 5.1 Grant SELECT and FLASHBACK on each captured table

**change** · **script:** `dba_cdc_03_cdc_setup.sql, Step 3`

Run in the PDB, as the privilege has to be given where the tables live.

Run in: SQL*Plus as SYSDBA, connected to the PDB

```sql
alter session set container = <pdb_name>;

grant select, flashback on EMOB.DISTRICT_INFO            to c##debezium;
grant select, flashback on EMOB.MB_ACCOUNT_DAILY_BALANCE to c##debezium;
grant select, flashback on EMOB.MB_ACCOUNT_MST           to c##debezium;
grant select, flashback on EMOB.MB_ACCOUNT_OPERATOR      to c##debezium;
grant select, flashback on EMOB.MB_ADDRESS_MST           to c##debezium;
grant select, flashback on EMOB.MB_CUSTOMER_MST          to c##debezium;
grant select, flashback on EMOB.MB_DOCUMENT_MST          to c##debezium;
grant select, flashback on EMOB.MB_PRODUCT_MST           to c##debezium;
grant select, flashback on EMOB.NOMINEE_MST              to c##debezium;
grant select, flashback on EMOB.STCODMAS                 to c##debezium;
grant select, flashback on EMOB.ST_AGENT_POINT           to c##debezium;
grant select, flashback on EMOB.ST_OPERATING_INSTRUCTION to c##debezium;
grant select, flashback on EMOB.ST_POINT_CATEGORY        to c##debezium;
grant select, flashback on EMOB.ST_SECTOR_CODE           to c##debezium;
grant select, flashback on EMOB.ST_TRANSACTION_CODE      to c##debezium;
grant select, flashback on EMOB.UNION_INFO               to c##debezium;
grant select, flashback on EMOB.UPAZILA_INFO             to c##debezium;
```

**Expected:** 17 grants succeed.

- The user must exist first ([step 4.1](#s4-1)).

[Back to contents](#contents)

<a id="s6"></a>
## 6. Supplemental log groups

Per-table logging of only the columns CDC needs. This replaces ALL COLUMNS logging, which writes every column of every changed row into the redo and fills the archive area for no benefit.

<a id="s6-1"></a>
### 6.1 Add one supplemental log group per captured table

**change** · **when:** After [step 3.1](#s3-1) and [step 5.1](#s5-1). Run it in a quiet period · **script:** `dba_cdc_03_cdc_setup.sql, Step 4`

Each group holds the row key plus the columns the downstream consumer uses to find related records. ALWAYS means those columns are logged on every update of the row, not only when one of them changes.

Run in: SQL*Plus as SYSDBA, connected to the PDB

```sql
alter session set container = <pdb_name>;

alter table EMOB.DISTRICT_INFO            add supplemental log group group_cdc_kafka_district_info (DISTRICT_CODE_GOV, DISTRICT_CODE) always;
alter table EMOB.MB_ACCOUNT_DAILY_BALANCE add supplemental log group group_cdc_kafka_mb_account_daily_balance (AC_ID, VALUE_DATE) always;
alter table EMOB.MB_ACCOUNT_MST           add supplemental log group group_cdc_kafka_mb_account_mst (AC_NO, AC_ID) always;
alter table EMOB.MB_ACCOUNT_OPERATOR      add supplemental log group group_cdc_kafka_mb_account_operator (AC_ID, CUST_NO, STATUS) always;
alter table EMOB.MB_ADDRESS_MST           add supplemental log group group_cdc_kafka_mb_address_mst (ADDRESS_ID, REF_NO) always;
alter table EMOB.MB_CUSTOMER_MST          add supplemental log group group_cdc_kafka_mb_customer_mst (CUST_NO) always;
alter table EMOB.MB_DOCUMENT_MST          add supplemental log group group_cdc_kafka_mb_document_mst (DOCUMENT_ID, CUST_NO) always;
alter table EMOB.MB_PRODUCT_MST           add supplemental log group group_cdc_kafka_mb_product_mst (AC_TYPE_ID) always;
alter table EMOB.NOMINEE_MST              add supplemental log group group_cdc_kafka_nominee_mst (NOMINEE_ID, AC_ID) always;
alter table EMOB.STCODMAS                 add supplemental log group group_cdc_kafka_stcodmas (HARCOD, SOFCOD) always;
alter table EMOB.ST_AGENT_POINT           add supplemental log group group_cdc_kafka_st_agent_point (POINT_ID) always;
alter table EMOB.ST_OPERATING_INSTRUCTION add supplemental log group group_cdc_kafka_st_operating_instruction (OPR_INS) always;
alter table EMOB.ST_POINT_CATEGORY        add supplemental log group group_cdc_kafka_st_point_category (POINT_CATEGORY_ID) always;
alter table EMOB.ST_SECTOR_CODE           add supplemental log group group_cdc_kafka_st_sector_code (SRLNO) always;
alter table EMOB.ST_TRANSACTION_CODE      add supplemental log group group_cdc_kafka_st_transaction_code (TRAN_CODE) always;
alter table EMOB.UNION_INFO               add supplemental log group group_cdc_kafka_union_info (UNION_CODE_GOV, DISTRICT_CODE, UPAZILA_CODE, UNION_CODE) always;
alter table EMOB.UPAZILA_INFO             add supplemental log group group_cdc_kafka_upazila_info (UPAZILA_CODE_GOV, DISTRICT_CODE, UPAZILA_CODE) always;
```

**Expected:** 17 statements succeed. Verify in [step 7.1](#s7-1).

- Applies to redo written from now on. Changes made before this step carry only the changed columns.
- Group names are unique per schema, so each table has its own name (g_cdc_kafka_ followed by the table name).
- Do not use ADD SUPPLEMENTAL LOG DATA (ALL) COLUMNS on these tables.

[Back to contents](#contents)

<a id="s6-2"></a>
### 6.2 Change the columns of an existing group, or add a table

**change** · **when:** Only when the captured columns or tables change

A log group cannot be edited. Drop it and add it again with the new column list.

Run in: SQL*Plus as SYSDBA, connected to the PDB

```sql
alter session set container = <pdb_name>;

-- example: add a column to MB_CUSTOMER_MST
alter table EMOB.MB_CUSTOMER_MST drop supplemental log group g_cdc_kafka_mb_customer_mst;
alter table EMOB.MB_CUSTOMER_MST add supplemental log group g_cdc_kafka_mb_customer_mst (CUST_NO, <new_column>) always;
```

- For a new table, also run [step 5.1](#s5-1) for it and add it to the connector's table.include.list ([step 9.1](#s9-1)).

[Back to contents](#contents)

<a id="s7"></a>
## 7. Verify the setup

Read-only. Run it after sections 3 to 6 and keep the output as the hand-over evidence.

<a id="s7-1"></a>
### 7.1 Check the user, log groups, table grants and database flags

**read-only** · **script:** `dba_cdc_03_cdc_setup.sql, Step 5`

Four queries, each with its expected result.

Run in: SQL*Plus as SYSDBA, connected to the PDB

```sql
alter session set container = ORCLPDB1;
set linesize 200 pagesize 100
col username format a14
col account_status format a16
col table_name format a28
col log_group_name format a32
col log_group_type format a18

-- 1. the CDC user
select username, account_status from dba_users where username = upper('c##debezium');

-- 2. the log groups
select table_name, log_group_name, log_group_type, always
  from dba_log_groups
 where owner = 'EMOB'
 order by table_name;

-- 3. the table grants
select count(*) as tables_granted
  from dba_tab_privs
 where grantee = upper('c##debezium') and owner = 'EMOB' and privilege = 'SELECT'
   and table_name in ('DISTRICT_INFO','MB_ACCOUNT_DAILY_BALANCE','MB_ACCOUNT_MST','MB_ACCOUNT_OPERATOR','MB_ADDRESS_MST','MB_CUSTOMER_MST','MB_DOCUMENT_MST','MB_PRODUCT_MST','NOMINEE_MST','STCODMAS','ST_AGENT_POINT','ST_OPERATING_INSTRUCTION','ST_POINT_CATEGORY','ST_SECTOR_CODE','ST_TRANSACTION_CODE','UNION_INFO','UPAZILA_INFO');

-- 4. the database flags
select supplemental_log_data_min as sup_min, supplemental_log_data_all as sup_all, force_logging, log_mode
  from v$database;
```

**Expected:** 1) the user, ACCOUNT_STATUS = OPEN. 2) 18 rows, LOG_GROUP_TYPE = USER LOG GROUP, ALWAYS = ALWAYS. 3) 18. 4) SUP_MIN = YES, SUP_ALL = NO, FORCE_LOGGING = YES, LOG_MODE = ARCHIVELOG.

- SUP_ALL = NO is correct: it confirms nobody enabled ALL COLUMNS logging at database level.
- The archive destination was already checked in [step 2.1](#s2-1).

[Back to contents](#contents)

<a id="s7-2"></a>
### 7.2 Check every privilege of the CDC user

**read-only** · **script:** `dba_cdc_06_check_cdc_privileges.sql`

One row per requirement, problems first: the user in both containers, the 22 LogMiner privileges in CDB$ROOT and in the PDB, quota for Debezium's LOG_MINING_FLUSH table, and SELECT and FLASHBACK on each captured table.


**dba_cdc_06_check_cdc_privileges.sql**  -  DOES THE DEBEZIUM USER HAVE EVERYTHING IT NEEDS?   (read-only)

   Run as   : sqlplus / as sysdba @dba_cdc_06_check_cdc_privileges.sql      (connected to CDB$ROOT)

   Checks   : 
    
	1. the user exists and is OPEN in CDB$ROOT and in the PDB

        2. every privilege granted in CDB$ROOT and in the PDB

                 (CONTAINER = ALL grants must reach both). Privileges inherited through a role also count.

         3. quota on the default tablespace in the PDB (Debezium creates its LOG_MINING_FLUSH table there)

         4. SELECT and FLASHBACK on each captured table in the PDB

              One row per check, problems first: MISSING / NO TABLE, then OK / VIA ROLE.

   Changes  : nothing. Safe on production.

   Edit     : the DEFINEs below, and the table list in section 3 if the captured tables change and save this whole as the **dba_cdc_06_check_cdc_privileges.sql** .


```bash
cat > dba_cdc_06_check_cdc_privileges.sql <<'EOF'
SET ECHO OFF  VERIFY OFF  DEFINE ON  FEEDBACK OFF  LINESIZE 200  PAGESIZE 200  TRIMSPOOL ON
WHENEVER SQLERROR EXIT FAILURE

-- cdc_user: the connector's database.user, pdb_name: its database.pdb.name, schema: owner of the tables (all upper case)
DEFINE cdc_user = 'C##DEBEZIUM' --change here
DEFINE pdb_name = 'ORCLPDB1' --change here
DEFINE schema   = 'EMOB' --change here

ALTER SESSION SET CONTAINER = CDB$ROOT;

-- Guard: the CDB_* views only show the PDB to SYSDBA (or a user with CONTAINER_DATA = ALL). Without it every
-- PDB check would wrongly report MISSING / NO TABLE, so stop instead.
BEGIN
  FOR r IN (SELECT 1 FROM dual WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v$containers WHERE name = '&pdb_name' AND open_mode LIKE 'READ%')) LOOP
    RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR(-20006, 'PDB &pdb_name is not visible or not open in this session - run as SYSDBA (sqlplus / as sysdba)');
  END LOOP;
END;
/

COLUMN container      FORMAT A10
COLUMN kind           FORMAT A8
COLUMN check_on       FORMAT A48
COLUMN status         FORMAT A8
COLUMN username       FORMAT A14
COLUMN account_status FORMAT A16
COLUMN detail         FORMAT A60

PROMPT
PROMPT ===== 1. The user =====================================================================
SELECT c.name AS container, NVL(u.username, '&cdc_user') AS username, NVL(u.account_status, '(does not exist)') AS account_status, u.common,
       CASE WHEN u.account_status = 'OPEN' THEN 'OK' ELSE 'MISSING' END AS status
  FROM v$containers c LEFT JOIN cdb_users u ON u.con_id = c.con_id AND u.username = '&cdc_user'
 WHERE c.name IN ('CDB$ROOT', '&pdb_name')
 ORDER BY c.con_id;

PROMPT
PROMPT ===== 2. Privileges needed in CDB$ROOT and in &pdb_name ==============================
WITH expected (kind, priv, obj) AS (
            SELECT 'SYSTEM', 'CREATE SESSION',          NULL FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'SYSTEM', 'SET CONTAINER',           NULL FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'SYSTEM', 'LOGMINING',               NULL FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'SYSTEM', 'SELECT ANY TRANSACTION',  NULL FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'SYSTEM', 'CREATE TABLE',            NULL FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'SYSTEM', 'CREATE SEQUENCE',         NULL FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'ROLE',   'SELECT_CATALOG_ROLE',     NULL FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'ROLE',   'EXECUTE_CATALOG_ROLE',    NULL FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'OBJECT', 'EXECUTE', 'DBMS_LOGMNR'          FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'OBJECT', 'EXECUTE', 'DBMS_LOGMNR_D'        FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'OBJECT', 'SELECT',  'V_$DATABASE'          FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'OBJECT', 'SELECT',  'V_$LOG'               FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'OBJECT', 'SELECT',  'V_$LOG_HISTORY'       FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'OBJECT', 'SELECT',  'V_$LOGFILE'           FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'OBJECT', 'SELECT',  'V_$ARCHIVED_LOG'      FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'OBJECT', 'SELECT',  'V_$ARCHIVE_DEST_STATUS' FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'OBJECT', 'SELECT',  'V_$LOGMNR_LOGS'       FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'OBJECT', 'SELECT',  'V_$LOGMNR_CONTENTS'   FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'OBJECT', 'SELECT',  'V_$LOGMNR_PARAMETERS' FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'OBJECT', 'SELECT',  'V_$TRANSACTION'       FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'OBJECT', 'SELECT',  'V_$MYSTAT'            FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'OBJECT', 'SELECT',  'V_$STATNAME'          FROM dual
), cons AS (
  SELECT con_id, name FROM v$containers WHERE name IN ('CDB$ROOT', '&pdb_name')
), roles AS (          -- every role the user holds in each container, including roles granted to those roles
  SELECT DISTINCT con_id, granted_role AS role FROM cdb_role_privs
   START WITH grantee = '&cdc_user'
   CONNECT BY NOCYCLE PRIOR granted_role = grantee AND PRIOR con_id = con_id
), holders AS (        -- direct = the user itself, via = one of its roles
  SELECT con_id, '&cdc_user' AS grantee, 'direct' AS how FROM cons
  UNION ALL SELECT con_id, role, 'via' FROM roles
), found AS (
  SELECT c.name AS container, e.kind, e.priv, e.obj,
         (SELECT MIN(h.how) FROM holders h WHERE h.con_id = c.con_id AND (
              (e.kind = 'SYSTEM' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cdb_sys_privs p WHERE p.con_id = c.con_id AND p.grantee = h.grantee AND p.privilege = e.priv))
           OR (e.kind = 'ROLE'   AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cdb_role_privs r WHERE r.con_id = c.con_id AND r.grantee = h.grantee AND r.granted_role = e.priv))
           OR (e.kind = 'OBJECT' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cdb_tab_privs t WHERE t.con_id = c.con_id AND t.grantee = h.grantee
                                              AND t.owner = 'SYS' AND t.table_name = e.obj AND t.privilege = e.priv))
         )) AS how
    FROM expected e CROSS JOIN cons c
)
SELECT container, kind,
       CASE WHEN obj IS NULL THEN priv ELSE priv || ' ON ' || obj END AS check_on,
       CASE how WHEN 'direct' THEN 'OK' WHEN 'via' THEN 'VIA ROLE' ELSE 'MISSING' END AS status
  FROM found
 ORDER BY CASE WHEN how IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, container, kind, check_on;

PROMPT
PROMPT ===== 3. Space for Debezium's LOG_MINING_FLUSH table (in &pdb_name) ===================
-- With database.pdb.name set, Debezium creates this table in the PDB, in the user's default tablespace there.
SELECT '&pdb_name' AS container,
       'default tablespace ' || u.default_tablespace AS check_on,
       CASE
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cdb_ts_quotas q WHERE q.con_id = u.con_id AND q.username = u.username
                        AND q.tablespace_name = u.default_tablespace AND (q.max_bytes = -1 OR q.max_bytes > q.bytes)) THEN 'OK'
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cdb_sys_privs p WHERE p.con_id = u.con_id AND p.grantee = u.username AND p.privilege = 'UNLIMITED TABLESPACE') THEN 'OK'
         ELSE 'MISSING'
       END AS status,
       CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cdb_tables t WHERE t.con_id = u.con_id AND t.owner = u.username AND t.table_name = 'LOG_MINING_FLUSH')
            THEN 'LOG_MINING_FLUSH exists: the connector has started at least once'
            ELSE 'LOG_MINING_FLUSH not created yet (made at the connector''s first start)' END AS detail
  FROM cdb_users u
 WHERE u.username = '&cdc_user' AND u.con_id = (SELECT con_id FROM v$containers WHERE name = '&pdb_name');

PROMPT
PROMPT ===== 4. SELECT and FLASHBACK on the captured tables in &pdb_name =====================
WITH tabs (table_name) AS (
            SELECT 'MB_ACCOUNT_MST'           FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'UNION_INFO'               FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'UPAZILA_INFO'             FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'DISTRICT_INFO'            FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'MB_ACCOUNT_DAILY_BALANCE' FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'MB_ACCOUNT_OPERATOR'      FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'MB_ADDRESS_MST'           FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'MB_CUSTOMER_MST'          FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'MB_DOCUMENT_MST'          FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'MB_PRODUCT_MST'           FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'STCODMAS'                 FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'ST_AGENT_POINT'           FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'ST_OPERATING_INSTRUCTION' FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'ST_POINT_CATEGORY'        FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'ST_SECTOR_CODE'           FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'ST_TRANSACTION_CODE'      FROM dual
  UNION ALL SELECT 'NOMINEE_MST'              FROM dual
), privs (priv) AS (SELECT 'SELECT' FROM dual UNION ALL SELECT 'FLASHBACK' FROM dual
), pdb AS (SELECT con_id FROM v$containers WHERE name = '&pdb_name'
), result AS (
  SELECT '&pdb_name' AS container, 'TABLE' AS kind, p.priv || ' ON &schema..' || t.table_name AS check_on,
         CASE
           WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cdb_tables x, pdb WHERE x.con_id = pdb.con_id AND x.owner = '&schema' AND x.table_name = t.table_name) THEN 'NO TABLE'
           WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cdb_tab_privs g, pdb WHERE g.con_id = pdb.con_id AND g.grantee = '&cdc_user'
                          AND g.owner = '&schema' AND g.table_name = t.table_name AND g.privilege = p.priv) THEN 'OK'
           ELSE 'MISSING'
         END AS status
    FROM tabs t CROSS JOIN privs p
)
SELECT container, kind, check_on, status FROM result ORDER BY status, check_on;

PROMPT
PROMPT ===== How to read the result ==========================================================
PROMPT OK / VIA ROLE : present (VIA ROLE = inherited through a role, which Debezium can use).
PROMPT MISSING       : re-run that GRANT from dba_cdc_03_cdc_setup.sql.
PROMPT                 OK in CDB$ROOT but MISSING in the PDB = granted without CONTAINER = ALL.
PROMPT                 Quota MISSING = ALTER USER &cdc_user QUOTA UNLIMITED ON <default tablespace> CONTAINER = ALL;
PROMPT NO TABLE      : the table does not exist in the PDB (check the name and the schema).
EOF


```

save this codebase as **dba_cdc_06_check_cdc_privileges.sql** and then run in: Shell on the database server, as oracle

```bash
sqlplus / as sysdba @dba_cdc_06_check_cdc_privileges.sql
```

**Expected:** Every row OK or VIA ROLE. Section 3 says LOG_MINING_FLUSH exists once the connector has started at least once.

- It must run as SYSDBA; as any other user, it stops with ORA-20006 because the PDB checks would be incorrect.
- OK in CDB$ROOT but MISSING in the PDB: the GRANT was given without CONTAINER = ALL. Re-run it from [step 4.2](#s4-2).
- Quota MISSING: ALTER USER c##debezium QUOTA UNLIMITED ON USERS CONTAINER = ALL;
- Section 4 of the script lists the 17 captured tables. Edit its table list when the captured tables change.

<a id="s7-3"></a>
### 7.3 Test that LogMiner captures changes on the captured tables

**read-only** · **script:** `dba_cdc_07_logminer_capture_test.sql`

Does what Debezium does, as the CDC user: adds the recent archive and online redo logs to a LogMiner session, starts it, and counts committed changes per captured table, with sample redo.

Run in: Optional, so there is something to find: one no-op change as the schema owner, in another session

```sql
alter session set container = ORCLPDB1;
update EMOB.ST_OPERATING_INSTRUCTION set OPR_INS = OPR_INS where rownum = 1;
commit;
```

Run in: Edit the DEFINE lines at the top of the script

```sql
cat > dba_cdc_07_logminer_capture_test.sql <<'EOF'
SET ECHO OFF  VERIFY OFF  DEFINE ON  FEEDBACK OFF  LINESIZE 220  PAGESIZE 200  TRIMSPOOL ON  SERVEROUTPUT ON
WHENEVER SQLERROR EXIT FAILURE

-- pdb_name: PDB that holds the schema (upper case), schema: owner of the captured tables, minutes: how far back to mine
DEFINE pdb_name = 'ORCLPDB1' --change here
DEFINE schema   = 'EMOB' --change here if needed
DEFINE minutes  = 60

/* ---- 0. Optional: make one test change first (as the schema owner, in the PDB, in ANOTHER session) ----------
   It changes no data: the column is set to its own value. Then run this script.
     ALTER SESSION SET CONTAINER = ORCLPDB1;
     UPDATE EMOB.ST_OPERATING_INSTRUCTION SET OPR_INS = OPR_INS WHERE ROWNUM = 1;
     COMMIT;
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

PROMPT
PROMPT ===== 1. Prerequisites ================================================================
COLUMN log_mode FORMAT A12
COLUMN sup_min  FORMAT A8
SELECT log_mode, supplemental_log_data_min AS sup_min, force_logging,
       CASE WHEN log_mode = 'ARCHIVELOG' AND supplemental_log_data_min IN ('YES', 'IMPLICIT') THEN 'OK' ELSE 'PROBLEM' END AS status
  FROM v$database;

PROMPT
PROMPT ===== 2. Start a LogMiner session over the last &minutes minutes ======================
DECLARE
  opt     PLS_INTEGER := DBMS_LOGMNR.NEW;
  n_arch  PLS_INTEGER := 0;
  n_redo  PLS_INTEGER := 0;
BEGIN
  -- archive logs that overlap the window, from one LOCAL destination (each sequence once)
  FOR r IN (SELECT name FROM v$archived_log
             WHERE dest_id = (SELECT MIN(dest_id) FROM v$archive_dest_status WHERE type = 'LOCAL' AND status = 'VALID')
               AND deleted = 'NO' AND status = 'A' AND name IS NOT NULL
               AND next_time > SYSDATE - &minutes / 1440
             ORDER BY thread#, sequence#) LOOP
    DBMS_LOGMNR.ADD_LOGFILE(LOGFILENAME => r.name, OPTIONS => opt);
    opt := DBMS_LOGMNR.ADDFILE;
    n_arch := n_arch + 1;
  END LOOP;
  -- online redo logs not archived yet, including the CURRENT one: the newest changes are only here
  FOR r IN (SELECT MIN(f.member) AS member FROM v$log l JOIN v$logfile f ON f.group# = l.group#
             WHERE l.archived = 'NO' GROUP BY l.group#) LOOP
    DBMS_LOGMNR.ADD_LOGFILE(LOGFILENAME => r.member, OPTIONS => opt);
    opt := DBMS_LOGMNR.ADDFILE;
    n_redo := n_redo + 1;
  END LOOP;
  DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE('logs added: ' || n_arch || ' archived, ' || n_redo || ' online');
  DBMS_LOGMNR.START_LOGMNR(STARTTIME => SYSDATE - &minutes / 1440,
                           OPTIONS   => DBMS_LOGMNR.DICT_FROM_ONLINE_CATALOG + DBMS_LOGMNR.COMMITTED_DATA_ONLY);
  DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE('LogMiner started: OK');
END;
/

PROMPT
PROMPT ===== 3. Committed changes LogMiner sees on the captured tables ======================
COLUMN table_name FORMAT A28
COLUMN operation  FORMAT A10
COLUMN first_seen FORMAT A19
COLUMN last_seen  FORMAT A19
SELECT table_name, operation, COUNT(*) AS changes,
       TO_CHAR(MIN(timestamp), 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS') AS first_seen,
       TO_CHAR(MAX(timestamp), 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS') AS last_seen
  FROM v$logmnr_contents
 WHERE src_con_name = '&pdb_name' AND seg_owner = '&schema'
   AND operation IN ('INSERT', 'UPDATE', 'DELETE')
   AND table_name IN ('MB_ACCOUNT_MST','UNION_INFO','UPAZILA_INFO','DISTRICT_INFO','MB_ACCOUNT_DAILY_BALANCE',
                      'MB_ACCOUNT_OPERATOR','MB_ADDRESS_MST','MB_CUSTOMER_MST','MB_DOCUMENT_MST','MB_PRODUCT_MST',
                      'STCODMAS','ST_AGENT_POINT','ST_OPERATING_INSTRUCTION','ST_POINT_CATEGORY','ST_SECTOR_CODE',
                      'ST_TRANSACTION_CODE','NOMINEE_MST')
 GROUP BY table_name, operation
 ORDER BY table_name, operation;

PROMPT
PROMPT ===== 4. Sample UPDATE redo (the log-group columns should appear in the WHERE part) ====
COLUMN sql_redo FORMAT A200 WORD_WRAPPED
SELECT table_name, SUBSTR(sql_redo, 1, 400) AS sql_redo
  FROM (SELECT table_name, sql_redo FROM v$logmnr_contents
         WHERE src_con_name = '&pdb_name' AND seg_owner = '&schema' AND operation = 'UPDATE'
         ORDER BY timestamp DESC)
 WHERE ROWNUM <= 3;

EXECUTE DBMS_LOGMNR.END_LOGMNR;

PROMPT
PROMPT ===== How to read the result ==========================================================
PROMPT Section 2 "LogMiner started: OK" : the user can run LogMiner (LOGMINING, DBMS_LOGMNR, V$ views are fine).
PROMPT Section 3 has rows               : LogMiner captures changes on those tables - Debezium will see them.
PROMPT Section 3 has no rows            : no committed change in the window. Make a test change (section 0) and re-run.
PROMPT Section 4 WHERE part             : must contain the log-group columns (for example CUST_NO), not only ROWID.
PROMPT ORA-01291 / ORA-01284            : a needed log file is missing on disk - check the archive cleanup.
PROMPT ORA-01031                        : missing privilege - run dba_cdc_06_check_cdc_privileges.sql.
EOF


```

Save this as Run in: Any machine with sqlplus, as the CDC user (this also proves its privileges are enough)

```bash
sqlplus '<debezium user name>@//<db_ip>:<port>/<service>' @dba_cdc_07_logminer_capture_test.sql 
```

**Expected:** Section 2 prints "LogMiner started: OK". Section 3 lists the changed tables with their change counts. Section 4 shows UPDATE redo whose WHERE part contains the log-group columns (for example AC_ID, AC_NO), not only ROWID. 
A password will be prompted, so give the password for debezium user

- No rows in section 3: nothing was committed on those tables in the window. Make the optional change above, or raise the window, and run again.
- ORA-01291 or ORA-01284: a log file LogMiner needs is no longer on disk. Check the cleanup in [step 10.1](#s10-1).
- ORA-01031: a privilege is missing. Run [step 7.2](#s7-2).
- If everything all right debezium is being able to capture all changes through logminer

<a id="s8"></a>
## 8. Monitoring user (optional)

Needed only for the Grafana dashboards. A separate read-only user that cannot read application data.

<a id="s8-1"></a>
### 8.1 Create the read-only monitoring user

**change** · **when:** Only if Grafana monitoring is being set up · **script:** `dba_cdc_04_monitoring_user.sql`

Lets the Oracle exporter read archive log, recovery area and database state views.

Run in: SQL*Plus as SYSDBA, connected to CDB$ROOT

```sql
alter session set container = CDB$ROOT;

create user c##cdcmon identified by "<password>" container = all;
grant create session, set container to c##cdcmon container = all;

grant select on v_$database            to c##cdcmon container = all;
grant select on v_$instance            to c##cdcmon container = all;
grant select on v_$pdbs                to c##cdcmon container = all;
grant select on v_$recovery_file_dest  to c##cdcmon container = all;
grant select on v_$recovery_area_usage to c##cdcmon container = all;
grant select on v_$archive_dest_status to c##cdcmon container = all;
grant select on v_$archived_log        to c##cdcmon container = all;
grant select on v_$log_history         to c##cdcmon container = all;

select username, account_status from dba_users where username = upper('c##cdcmon');
```

**Expected:** ACCOUNT_STATUS = OPEN.

- Hand the user and password to whoever runs Grafana. Setup of the exporter is in monitoring/README.md.

<a id="s9"></a>
## 9. Hand-off to the connector [Not Needed for Now]

What the Debezium connector needs from this setup. The connector itself is registered by the platform team.

<a id="s9-1"></a>
### 9.1 Values to give the platform team

**read-only**

These must match what you created, or the connector fails to log in or captures the wrong tables.

Run in: For reference: the connector settings these values go into Debeziums config file

```bash
database.user           = c##debezium
database.password       = <the CDC user's password>
database.dbname         = <CDB name: select name from v$database>
database.pdb.name       = ORCLPDB1
table.include.list      = EMOB.DISTRICT_INFO,EMOB.MB_ACCOUNT_DAILY_BALANCE,EMOB.MB_ACCOUNT_MST,EMOB.MB_ACCOUNT_OPERATOR,EMOB.MB_ADDRESS_MST,EMOB.MB_CUSTOMER_MST,EMOB.MB_DOCUMENT_MST,EMOB.MB_PRODUCT_MST,EMOB.NOMINEE_MST,EMOB.STCODMAS,EMOB.ST_AGENT_POINT,EMOB.ST_OPERATING_INSTRUCTION,EMOB.ST_POINT_CATEGORY,EMOB.ST_SECTOR_CODE,EMOB.ST_TRANSACTION_CODE,EMOB.UNION_INFO,EMOB.UPAZILA_INFO
```

- The user name is case-sensitive in the connector config. Use the name exactly as created.
- table.include.list holds the 17 captured tables. MB_TRANSACTION_DTL has its grant and log group but is excluded from the connector in this phase.
- A new table needs a grant ([step 5.1](#s5-1)), a log group ([step 6.1](#s6-1)) and an entry in table.include.list.
- With snapshot.mode = no_data only changes made after the connector starts are captured, and only when committed.
